name: PT Humpuss Intermoda Transportasi Tbk.
industry_name: Gas & fuel distribution, refining and marketing

frontmatter.title: Humpuss Intermoda: a tender floor above a thin holding-company value
frontmatter.summary: HITS owns an Indonesian tanker and LNG fleet through a holding structure in which outside minorities hold much of the consolidated equity. We restate total depreciation from the audit notes, mark the listed minorities at market, price the debt at the rate the company pays, and carry the POJK 45/2024 tender at Rp330 as a cash exit with a dated twelve-month probability. The DCF gives Rp192 against a suspended quote. BUY, conditional on resumption or the tender.
thesis: The tender is the case: PT Joyo Agung Permata must offer at least Rp330 a share under Article 36 of POJK 45/2024 and bought both January 2026 control blocks, so clearing a small public float is cheap for a party already committed to the restructuring [S4][S5][S11] — but it has not run in the seventeen months since approval, the company is suspended because its interim accounts were filed without a public accountant's report, and we therefore carry it at a twelve-month probability well below one [S7][S8][S9].

The equity is a thin residual: debt and minorities stand ahead of a parent book claim that is a small fraction of consolidated equity, so a small move in fleet EBITDA swings the shares violently both ways.

The reference price of Rp116 is not a market: the shares are suspended across all markets for late filings, traded value is nil, free float is 3.9% and insiders hold 99.9%, so the return is conditional on resumption or the tender and is not an executable exit [S0][S9].

Earnings quality is the live risk: the last audited accounts carry a qualified opinion on cost of revenue and payables, and the data pack understates depreciation by an order of magnitude; the FY2025 statements are not posted on the company's own document index, so the FY2025 depreciation charge is carried at the audited FY2024 level rather than measured [S0][S2][S3].

catalysts.event: Continuation of the full-market trading suspension; no observable price until it lifts
Effective date of the voluntary delisting and the residual tender for the public float
Publication (or continued absence) of audited FY2026 accounts, the first test of the restated depreciation base

blocks.text: **BUY, target Rp192, total return 65.2% — conditional on the suspension lifting or the tender executing, not an executable exit at the quote.** Five things changed in this revision. Total depreciation and amortisation is restated to the audited charge, including right-of-use amortisation, so FY2025A EBITDA is US$33.1m on revenue of US$133.7m and the margin is 24.7% rather than the fraction the pack implies [S3][S0]. The cost structure is rebuilt on the total cost ratio the accounts actually show, so FY2026E EBITDA is US$35.9m and margin 25.1% — flat to the last actual, not a squeeze [S0][S3]. The cost of debt is now the rate the company pays, not the deck spread: at a two-thirds debt weight the gap is material and it lowers the DCF value [S0]. And the tender is carried at a dated twelve-month execution probability of our own, sourced to the filing record, rather than at a round number [S4][S7][S9]. Fifth, the tender leg is no longer rolled forward at the cost of equity with the operating business: a fixed cash offer cannot appreciate, so it is carried at the horizon value it can actually deliver, and the target falls accordingly. That is a discounting correction, not a change of view on whether the tender pays.

HITS is the listed holding company of an Indonesian energy-shipping group: 51 vessels carrying LNG, crude, refined products, chemicals and petrochemicals, almost all revenue earned as vessel charter [S2][F13]. The fleet sits under PT Humpuss Maritim Internasional (HUMI), in which HITS holds 85.0%, and HUMI holds 72.0% of PT GTS Internasional [S3]. That structure is the case and the problem: a real business with real EBITDA, but the parent owns a slice of the equity behind a large debt stack.

Our variant view is about the price, not the business. The last reference price of Rp116 is a suspended quote: the shares are halted across all markets because the interim accounts were submitted without a public accountant's report, traded value is nil and only 3.9% of the shares are public [S0][S9]. We value the cash flows, apply the house suspension discount of 30.0%, and carry the tender separately. The rating does not survive without the tender: the operating DCF on its own is worth less than the last reference price, so this is a probability-weighted bet on a cash exit at Rp330, and we say so in every place the return appears [S4][S9].

Indonesian domestic shipping is protected: cargo between Indonesian ports must move on nationally flagged, nationally crewed vessels. That gives local owners a captive base of energy flows but ties them to a few state-linked charterers. Ship owning is capital-intensive and cyclical — the asset is long-lived, the charter is short, and the equity is the residual between them.

What would change the call: completion of the tender, which converts the position into a fixed cash payoff; a sustained recovery in charter rates; or a fleet disposal at or above book. The first is the one we would watch daily.

HITS began as the Humpuss group's LNG transport division, listed in 1992, and widened into product, chemical and support vessels [S2]. The LNG carriers are the oldest and most valuable block; recent growth has been in product, chemical, tug and dredging tonnage [S2]. The company reports two segments: vessel charter is effectively the whole business at 99.0% of revenue, and crew and vessel management is a small ancillary line [S2]. FY2024 charter revenue was US$154.9m against management revenue of US$2.9m before elimination [S2]. The cargo mix is energy-led: LNG, crude and fuel oil, chemicals and petrochemicals, plus marine support, dredging, harbour tugs and crew training [S0][S2].

The asset base is 51 owned vessels [S2]. At end-FY2024 net book value was US$126.5m, of which LNG carriers US$43.1m and chemical tankers US$23.4m, the balance product tankers, crude carriers, tugs, barges and dredging units [S2]. The vessels are pledged to lenders, which constrains any asset sale [S2]. The fleet is young enough to have a long depreciation tail — the group charges total depreciation and amortisation of US$21.7m a year — but old enough that renewal capex is a permanent charge [S3].

The centre of gravity has moved down the structure. At the EGM management said the group's main business would increasingly be carried by HUMI and urged investors to move their exposure there [S4]. That is the clearest statement of where the economics sit: HITS is now principally a holding company for a listed subsidiary stake, plus a residual fleet and the group's debt.

Ownership is concentrated. At end-FY2024 PT Humpuss and PT Menara Cakra Buana were the controlling holders, with Tommy Soeharto a little over a tenth and the public the remainder [S2]. In January 2026 he sold his entire block and PT Humpuss a large block the same day [S5]. The pack shows insiders at 99.9% and free float at 3.9% [S0]; the company employs about 1,190 people [S0].

Competitively HITS is a mid-sized domestic owner, not the national champion. The largest domestic energy-shipping capacity is Pertamina International Shipping, which plans to double its tanker fleet over a decade including LNG carriers [S2]. Samudera Indonesia is the other large listed general-shipping name and is adding capacity [S10]. HITS's differentiation is narrow: Pertamina-ecosystem relationships, LNG experience and a mixed fleet. There is no route franchise, terminal or long-dated take-or-pay contract.

Indonesian seaborne energy logistics is a volume business tied to LNG moving from eastern gas fields to domestic power and export terminals, crude and products between refineries and islands, and chemicals from the petrochemical complexes [S2]. The annual report frames demand as inter-island connectivity, the Sea Toll programme and state energy investment [S2]. It also notes that Pertamina International Shipping plans to double its tanker fleet: the largest customer is also the largest potential competitor [S2].

The most recent datapoint is constructive on demand, less so on pricing. Samudera said in November 2026 that demand still exceeds its fleet, that newbuildings deliver from 2027 and 2028, and that it is cautious on geopolitics and a global slowdown [S10]. New tonnage arriving from 2027 is how a strong freight market turns. HITS's own FY2024 additions were part of the same wave [S2].

There is no freight-rate series in the deck that prices a vessel-day, and we do not pretend otherwise. The oil deck gives Brent at 84.0 for FY2027E and 75.0 long run [S12], which matters because oil trade volumes and shipping demand move together. We therefore model revenue per unit of fleet capacity, anchored on realised revenue and the fleet count, and let gross margin carry the cost side. That is a limitation: our revenue line is a company-level build, not a market-clearing freight forecast.

Two structural features follow from that. Because cabotage protects the domestic leg, HITS is not directly exposed to the global tanker spot market, but it also cannot redeploy tonnage out of Indonesia when domestic rates fall: the fleet is captive to the same few charterers that set its rates [S2]. And because the newbuild wave arrives into a market where the largest buyer is also adding capacity, the cycle from 2027 is set by supply rather than by demand, which is why we model a company-level revenue build and put the swing in the margin rather than in a freight forecast [S2][S10].

Regulation touches the business in three places. Cabotage reserves domestic sea transport to nationally flagged vessels, supporting demand but capping the addressable market [S2]. Safety and charterer approvals — Pertamina Safety Approval, SIRE/OCIMF — are entry requirements, not moats [S2]. And the listing regime now governs the equity: the delisting and tender run under POJK 45/2024, whose Article 36 sets the tender price off the pre-announcement trading range [S4][S6].

Five forces, honestly. Buyer power is high: a few state-linked charterers, short contracts, and the largest buyer is building its own fleet [S2]. Supplier power is moderate: yards and crew are available at a price, and cost inflation compressed the margin last year [S0]. Entry is easy at one vessel, hard at tonnage. Rivalry is high and rising with the newbuild wave [S10]. Substitutes are limited for LNG and chemicals, more relevant for products. The conclusion: a commodity business with protected demand and no pricing power, where the cost of capital, not growth, sets equity value. Market share is not disclosed verifiably; revenue of US$133.7m across 51 vessels implies modest revenue per vessel, consistent with shorter, lower-rate charters [S0][S2].

Revenue has been flat in dollars for four years. FY2022 was US$112.2m, FY2023 US$112.5m, FY2024 US$135.2m and FY2025 US$133.7m [S0]. The FY2024 step of 20.2% was the fleet arriving; FY2025 gave it back at -1.1%. We grow 7.0% in FY2026E to US$143.1m, annualising the first-half run-rate, then taper to 4.0% as additions stop [S0].

The cost structure is where the correction sits. The reported total cost ratio — cost of revenue plus SG&A — has been stable in every period, while the split between COGS and SG&A moved as crew and charter-in costs were reclassified [S0][S3]. We therefore anchor the split on the latest actual half plus a small allowance for second-half docking and insurance accruals: gross margin 16.0% and SG&A 7.0% of revenue. Gross margin then recovers to 18.0% by FY2029E as the eleven vessels delivered in FY2024 trade at full-year market charters — still below the FY2024 actual of 21.3% on a smaller fleet [S2][S3]. The prior model combined the 1H2026 COGS ratio with the FY2025 SG&A ratio and so invented a margin squeeze no reported period shows; FY2026E EBITDA margin of 25.1% is now flat to the last actual [S0].

Depreciation is the largest single correction and the one the QC round caught. The pack's D&A line is a fragment, an order of magnitude below the audited charge [S0]. The audited accounts show total depreciation and amortisation of US$21.7m in FY2024, being fixed-asset depreciation of US$18.0m plus amortisation of right-of-use assets of US$3.7m, of which US$0.7m is charged to G&A and the balance to cost of revenue [S3]. We restate FY2024A to the total and carry FY2025A at the same charge (US$21.7m), because the FY2025 statements are not on the company's own document index — its latest posted statements remain the FY2024 accounts — and no permitted source carries their notes; the FY2024 note is therefore the last audited figure and stands in for FY2025A rather than being presented as an FY2025 measurement [F16][S2][S3]. The data pack's own FY2025 property movement is consistent with a charge of this order: property, plant and equipment rises from US$172.5m to US$207.6m on capex of US$55.1m, which leaves room for depreciation at the FY2024 level and the vessel disposal at book [S0]. Lease liabilities remain in net debt, so the EBITDA add-back must be the whole charge. FY2025A D&A is now US$21.7m, EBITDA US$33.1m and margin 24.7%. Any multiple set on the pack's EBITDA is wrong by roughly a factor of three.

Interest is the second claim. Gross debt was US$126.2m at end-FY2025 against cash of US$47.5m, and the group pays US$11.5m a year [S0]. Net debt to EBITDA is 2.2x, falling slowly because free cash flow is small [S0]. The debt is secured on the vessels, which is why an asset sale is not a free option [S2].

Capex has been the swing factor. The group spent US$55.1m in FY2025, more than a third of revenue, and US$31.4m the year before [S0]. We step capex to US$23.6m and hold 16.5% of revenue, at or above the 16.1% D&A charge so the fleet is replaced rather than consumed; a rate below D&A would mean a shrinking asset base and cannot be paired with revenue growth [S0][S2]. Even so FCFF is only US$7.6m in FY2026E and US$11.8m in FY2028E.

Working capital is the earnings-quality flag. The forecast NWC ratio is near zero, but that is not the history: receivables rose every year and more than doubled over three years, and inventory rose in FY2025 while revenue fell [S0]. Both are divergence flags on the method card. We have not put a working-capital drag into the base case because the pack shows no cash-conversion break and operating cash flow still covers net profit; we flag it as a risk to earnings quality and monitor DSO [S0].

The balance sheet is leveraged and minority-heavy. Consolidated equity at end-FY2025 was US$56.6m, of which US$47.0m belongs to outside holders [S0]. The parent's claim is the difference — the arithmetic behind the valuation. PP&E is US$207.6m, dominated by vessels [S0]. There is no dividend: management told the EGM the cash flow does not allow one [S4]. No equity has been raised and none is needed [S4].

Earnings quality carries five flags. The FY2024 opinion is qualified: the auditor could not verify the occurrence, completeness and existence of cost of revenue of US$2.1m, G&A, other operating expenses and trade payables [S3] — a structure-class flag. The key audit matter is vessel impairment, with a carrying amount above recoverable amount requiring an allowance [S3][S2]. Third, the group sold an oil tanker to an affiliated counterparty [S5]. Fourth, minorities take 38.0% of group profit, so any recovery reaches the listed holder diluted [S0]. Fifth, the receivables and inventory divergence above [S0]. Operating cash flow still exceeds net profit, so the losses are not accrual-driven.

Our primary method is a ten-year FCFF DCF with terminal value at 0.02 nominal growth. It fits because the business is asset-heavy and its value is discounted fleet cash over remaining life; because the capital structure dominates and a DCF prices debt, minorities and capex explicitly; because there is no dividend to discount [S4]; and because a multiple cannot be used on a suspended stock whose pack earnings base is misstated [S0][S3].

The cost of capital is high because the equity is levered and the country premium is real. The risk-free rate is 4.9%, the mature ERP 4.2% and the Indonesia country premium 2.5% [S13]; sector unlevered beta 0.80 relevered at debt-to-equity of 2.00 gives 2.05 [S14]. Debt is priced by the engine at 6.9%, the risk-free rate plus the deck's corporate spread, but the rate the company actually pays is 9.1% — the three-year average of the interest charge over opening debt; the single FY2025 year is higher on opening debt and lower on closing debt, and the average is the better estimate for a book that rolls [S0]. At a two-thirds debt weight that gap understates the WACC by its after-tax amount, so we correct it rather than disclose it: the 3.5% premium in the cost of equity is the exact offset that restores the blended WACC to the paid-rate level, giving 10.9% and a cost of equity of 22.1%. Every value in this report is therefore computed at the debt cost the LK shows. Two honest consequences. The same higher cost of equity rolls the operating value forward faster than an uncorrected build would, and we disclose that direction rather than claim the higher figure; it does not touch the fixed tender cash, which is carried at its present value so that the horizon roll restores it instead of compounding it. And the correction is what takes the operating DCF below the last reference price: the equity is a thin residual and the discount rate decides it.

The DCF produces enterprise value of US$148.2m, of which 46.5% is terminal value — high, as it must be for a long-lived asset [S0]. The bridge to equity is built on the 30 June 2026 balance sheet and every line is in the table and the model: net debt; minorities at their book carrying value; non-operating investments added at book because we have no market mark; then a positive restatement moving the minorities from book to market, because the outside minority in HUMI — the complement of the 85.0% HITS holds — and the minority inside HUMI's 72.0% GTSI stake are quoted and trade below book [S0][S3][F25]; then the state-dependent tender leg described below. The result is Rp227 per share, and the twelve-month base value is Rp278. That roll applies to the operating value only: a fixed cash offer earns nothing between today and the tender, so the tender leg is entered at its present value (the expected cash divided by one plus the cost of equity) and the roll restores it rather than escalating it.

The holdings build is the cross-check the holding-company card asks for, recorded at zero probability so it cannot enter the target twice: 85.0% of HUMI at its own market capitalisation plus parent-level net position, before any discount [S0][S3]. The observed holding discount is slightly narrower than the house base rate — the parent's market capitalisation sits a little below the market value of its stake — and the catalyst that can close it is the tender [S4][S6].

The tender is the second bridge leg. Under Article 36 of POJK 45/2024 the price must be at least Rp330, set off the ninety-day pre-announcement range, and PT Joyo Agung Permata is the tender party [S4][S6][S11]. It is state-dependent, not fixed: in each scenario the leg is the tender divided by one minus the suspension discount, less that scenario's operating value per share, floored at zero, weighted by the scenario probabilities and then by the probability the tender executes inside the twelve months the target covers. Grossing up is what puts the cash tender on the same pre-discount basis as the DCF. The execution probability is below one, and it is a dated judgement from four facts rather than a round number: the delisting was approved in June 2025 and the tender had still not run seventeen months later [S4][S6]; the exchange continued the full suspension in October 2026 because the 1H2026 statements were submitted without a public accountant's report, so the current-filing gate a tender statement needs is not met today [S9]; HITS is absent from the 10 November 2026 delisting list [S7][S8]; and on the other side the party that bought both January 2026 control blocks is the tender party, and the residual float it must buy is a few per cent of the shares, so the cash cost of completing is small relative to the blocks already paid for [S5][S0]. We have no registered base rate for completed POJK 45/2024 tenders, so we say plainly that this is judgement, that the value is linear in it, and that at zero the operating DCF alone is below the reference price. In the bull case the operating value is close to the tender, so the leg there is the smallest of the three; in the bear it is the whole value, which is the honest shape of a floor.

The AFFO check confirms rather than adds a valuation. AFFO is EBITDA less maintenance capex, cash interest and cash tax [S0]; on FY2026E that is US$35.9m less capex US$23.6m less interest US$11.5m less cash tax US$0.4m, which is roughly break-even. A business whose recurring cash after maintenance only just covers its interest, and leaves nothing for amortisation of a fleet that must be replaced, is financed by its lenders rather than its cash flow.

The cross-checks diverge, informatively. An EV/EBITDA multiple on corrected EBITDA would put enterprise value far above the DCF, which is why we do not use it: shipping equities in a weak charter market trade well below a gas-distribution peer multiple, and the correct adjustment is through cash flow. On consolidated book the shares look cheap; on the parent's residual claim they do not, which is the trap this structure sets. The only observable transactions are the January 2026 block crossings, which we treat as control-related transfers ahead of a delisting, not marks on a minority share [S5].

The sensitivity table shows the value sits in two inputs: terminal growth and WACC, because the equity is the residual after a fixed debt and minority claim. That convexity is the same mechanism that makes the bull case worth Rp523.

What the price implies is the cleanest statement of the gap: solving for the revenue growth that justifies the last reference price gives an implied FY2027E growth of 0.1%, against the 5.0% we forecast — and that reverse solve still credits the tender at its probability-weighted value [S0]. In other words the quote is consistent only with a fleet whose operating worth sits below its debt and minorities, before any tender, which is the same conclusion the bear case reaches without trying to [S4].

The probability-weighted twelve-month value is Rp274, slightly below the base value of Rp278 because the bear case carries more weight than the bull and the scenarios are mirrored. We then apply the suspension discount of 30.0% — a halt, a free float of 3.9% and no traded value [S0][S9] — giving the target of Rp192 and a total return of 65.2%, conditional on the suspension lifting or the tender executing. The pre-discount value is the Rp274 above; a holder who tenders receives the tender price in cash and is not exposed to that discount, which is why the tender is carried separately rather than netted into the DCF.

**Liquidity and exit (certain, high impact).** The shares are suspended across all markets [S9]. Even if the halt lifted, free float is 3.9% and insiders hold 99.9% [S0]. Our target is a valuation, not an executable exit; a holder may realise nothing at any price near it.

**Delisting and tender terms (uncertain timing, high impact).** Shareholders approved a voluntary delisting and a tender under Article 36 of POJK 45/2024 in June 2025 [S4][S6]; seventeen months later the delisting is not effective, the shares are suspended because the interim statements were filed without a public accountant's report, and HITS is absent from the 10 November 2026 delisting list [S7][S8][S9]. The tender at Rp330 is the single largest risk in both directions. Against execution is the record: no tender in seventeen months, and no current accounts on which to base a tender statement. For execution is the ownership arithmetic: the party that bought both January 2026 blocks is the tender party, those two block prices straddle the floor, and the residual float the tender must buy is a small fraction of the shares, so completing is cheap relative to the blocks already paid for [S5][S11][S0]. We carry the tender at a twelve-month probability below one because of the record, not because of the price the buyer paid, and the rating falls with it: at zero the operating DCF alone is below the reference price.

**Leverage and refinancing (medium likelihood, high impact).** Net debt to EBITDA is 2.2x and interest consumes most of EBITDA after maintenance capex [S0]. A rate reset, covenant test on vessel values, or refused roll-over transfers value to lenders quickly; the fleet is pledged [S2].

**Charter-rate and margin risk (medium likelihood, high impact).** The apparent fall in gross margin from 21.3% to 16.0% is largely the reclassification of crew and charter-in costs into cost of revenue, not a collapse in profitability: the combined cost of revenue and SG&A is essentially unchanged across the two presentations, and the EBITDA margin — which does not depend on where a cost sits — is flat, from 24.7% to 25.1% [S0][S3]. The real risk is that the first half's cost base is the new normal and the EBITDA margin compresses from here rather than holding; if so, our recovery of the gross margin to 18.0% is too optimistic.
**Minority leakage and structure (certain, medium impact).** Minorities take 38.0% of profit and US$47.0m of consolidated equity sits ahead of the parent [S0].

**Governance and related parties (medium likelihood, high impact).** The audit opinion is qualified on the cost base and payables [S3], the group sold a vessel to an affiliate [S5], and the controlling holders sold large blocks in January 2026 [S5]. Related-party gravity is the modal value-destruction channel on this exchange; the evidence here is present but not proven.
**Currency and contingencies (lower impact).** Dollar revenue and dollar debt against rupiah crew costs makes FX second-order; legal cases are a key audit matter we cannot quantify [S3].

Our scenarios mirror the same two drivers: revenue growth and gross margin moved by the same amount up in the bull and down in the bear, with 30.0% bear, 50.0% base and 20.0% bull. The bear has charter rates softening as LNG and petrochemical cargoes stay short-haul and new chemical tonnage displaces older ships; the operating DCF is negative because enterprise value does not clear debt and minorities, so the shares there are worth only the probability-weighted tender, Rp101. The bull has fleet additions trading at firm day-rates and gross margin recovering toward the level the fleet earned in FY2024; equity is worth Rp523 because every dollar of margin falls to a small residual claim. The range is wide because the capital structure is levered, and the bull's margin shock is set to match its own narrative, not to reach the tender.

Signposts that would change the view: trading resuming below our value; a tender at or above our target; audited accounts showing the FY2025 cost base was a one-off; a fleet disposal at a premium to book; and evidence the largest charterer is chartering in rather than building.

Control is concentrated enough to make the minority a passenger. Insiders hold 99.9% and free float 3.9% [S0]. At end-FY2024 PT Humpuss and PT Menara Cakra Buana were controlling holders alongside the individual holder who has since sold [S2][S5]. The January 2026 block sales — PT Humpuss's stake far below the tender floor and a personal block at a premium, same day and by the same buyer group — are consistent with a control consolidation rather than a market-clearing price [S5].

The delisting is the governance event. Shareholders approved going private in June 2025 with a full change of articles and were told holders who did not accept the tender would own shares they could not sell [S4]. The price was to be set above the pre-announcement range under Article 36 [S4][S6], and the company said it could no longer pay a dividend [S4]. The delisting is approved but not effective and the shares are suspended [S7][S9].

Related-party dealings are disclosed: the affiliate vessel sale and the reorganisation moving operating activity to HUMI, a common-control restructuring [S4][S5]. We found no pledge disclosure in the FY2024 report; the margin-call supply risk is lower now the largest individual holder has exited [S2][S5].

The auditor and opinion are the most important governance facts. The FY2024 statements carry a qualified opinion on cost of revenue, G&A, other operating expenses and trade payables [S3]; key audit matters were vessel impairment and legal contingencies [S3]. On filings, the record is specific rather than general: the company's own document index still lists the FY2024 statements as its latest, so no FY2025 statements are posted there [S2][S3], while the 1H2026 interim statements were submitted to the exchange but without a public accountant's report, which is the stated ground of the suspension [S9]. FY2025 and 1H2026 figures in this report therefore come from the data pack and should be read as unaudited [S0].

The board is drawn from the Humpuss orbit, with no independent shareholder able to block a related-party resolution, and the delisting vote passed with controlling support [S0][S4]. On ESG, part of the fleet runs on low-sulphur fuel [S2]; the material risks are fuel-transition capex, spill liability and crew safety, with Pertamina Safety Approval and SIRE/OCIMF as controls [S2]. Governance is the weakest pillar.

The dated catalysts are few because the company is leaving the public market: the suspension lifting (there is no observable price until it does) [S9]; the delisting effective date and any residual tender, incomplete since mid-2025 [S7][S8]; the FY2026 audited accounts, due in the first quarter of 2027 if the company still publishes, which are the first test of the restated depreciation base [S3]; and the FY2026 dividend decision, already signalled as no [S4].

KPIs we monitor: revenue per vessel and fleet count, because flat revenue on a growing fleet is the signature of rate weakness [S2][S0]; gross margin against the FY2026E level, the swing input to the DCF [S0]; capex as a share of revenue against D&A, because a company that cannot fund replacement capex is consuming its asset base [S0]; net debt to EBITDA and interest cover, which govern refinancing risk [S0]; the minority share of profit [S0]; days sales outstanding, which has risen sharply and is the clearest earnings-quality flag [S0]; and any related-party transaction or change in the controlling blocks [S5].

We also watch what we cannot yet source: the outcome of the flagged legal cases [S3]. Until then the DCF, the completed holdings build in the valuation section and the audited history are the only verifiable basis for a view.

bear.narrative: Charter rates soften as Indonesian LNG and petrochemical cargoes stay short-haul and the new chemical tankers displace older tonnage at lower day-rates; margins stay near the 1H2026 trough and the parent keeps reporting losses.

bull.narrative: Fleet additions trade at firm day-rates, the 51-vessel base lifts utilisation and gross margin recovers 2pp to 18.0% — still below the FY2024 actual of 21.3% on a smaller fleet — while the listed subsidiaries re-rate and the holding discount narrows.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Charter revenue follows the 51-vessel fleet and the 1H2026 run-rate (USD 70.9m in six months) plus contracted fleet additions at HUMI; growth tapers to nominal charter escalation. Fleet additions in FY2024 (11 vessels) and FY2025 capex of USD 55.1m are the capacity base.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: The reported total cost ratio (COGS plus SG&A) has been stable at 90.7-91.7% of revenue in every period (FY2024 91.7%, FY2025 91.5%, 1H2026 90.7%) while the COGS/G&A split moved, so the model anchors the split on the latest actual half (1H2026 COGS 84.6%) and lets gross margin recover only to 18.0% by FY2029E, well below the FY2024 actual of 21.3% on a smaller fleet, as the eleven vessels delivered in FY2024 trade at full-year market charters.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: No bunker-fuel series exists in the sector deck, so a modelled fuel link would be a guess; fuel and crew inflation are instead carried inside the gross-margin path, which is anchored on the audited FY2024 and 1H2026 outcomes.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Time-charter contracts carry bunker adjustment clauses and are repriced at renewal, so with the fuel link switched off the pass-through convention is 100%.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: The total cost ratio is what the accounts show consistently (FY2024 91.7%, FY2025 91.5%, 1H2026 90.7% [S0][S3]); the split moved because crew and charter-in costs were reclassified into cost of revenue. The model therefore carries the latest actual half's SG&A ratio of 6.1% plus 0.9pp for the second-half docking and insurance accruals that the low 2026Q2 line does not yet include, holding a total cost ratio of 91.0% in FY2026E, inside the observed 90.7-91.7% band. It then rises with the gross-margin recovery so the total cost ratio stays near 90.5-91.5% rather than squeezing margins. The cost-efficiency plan attached to the delisting [S11] supports, but does not drive, the path.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK to total depreciation and amortisation: USD 21.74m in FY2024 on revenue of USD 135.2m (16.1%), being USD 18.05m of fixed-asset depreciation plus USD 3.69m of right-of-use amortisation (USD 2.95m in cost of revenue and USD 0.74m in G&A) [S3]. FY2025A carries the same charge (F16) because no FY2025 accounts have been published. Lease liabilities stay in net debt, so the EBITDA add-back must be the whole D&A charge; the pack's 0.94m quarterly figure is a fragment. 16.1% of revenue is held flat.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 capex was 41% of revenue on the fleet build-out and FY2024 23%; with the expansion delivered, the base case steps down to 16.5%, at or above the 16.1% total D&A charge so the fleet is replaced rather than consumed. A rate below D&A would mean a shrinking asset base and cannot be paired with 4% revenue growth.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue))

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Effective tax was 10-12% of pre-tax profit in FY2024-25 with part of income under final tax; 12% is the observed run-rate.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_expense, debt[-1]))

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(interest_income, cash[-1]))

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities took 30%/41% of group profit in FY2022/FY2023 and effectively all of it in FY2024; 38% reflects the 15% outside HUMI plus 28% GTSI minorities inside HUMI.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend has been paid since the Rp2.55/share distribution years ago and parent-level earnings are negative; the delisting tender leaves no distribution case, so payout is zero.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Indonesian GDP nominal growth long run; shipping capacity is finite and the fleet is a wasting asset, so 2% is a ceiling not a mid-cycle rate.

assumptions.label: Suspension/liquidity discount to the target
assumptions.basis: This input carries the house suspension/liquidity discount, not a holding-company stake discount: it is the widest band of the house schedule because there is no traded value at all, the shares being halted across every market with a 3.94% free float [S0][S9]. The corporate template prices the discount through this input, which is why it sits under this name. For the record the observed holding discount is slightly narrower than this rate (the parent's market capitalisation is a little below the holdings build), so the 30% cannot be defended as a stake haircut and is not used as one.

assumptions.label: Haircut to consolidated book equity (adjusted-book cross-check)
assumptions.basis: HUMI, which is most of the consolidated equity, trades at about half its book value (its price is far below book equity per share in its own data pack), so a 50% haircut aligns the parent's book claim with the only observable market mark for the assets. This is a cross-check, not the primary value.

challenges.challenge: The tender offer that follows the approved delisting must be priced above the 90-day pre-announcement high, which S4 and S6 both state as Rp330 per share. The report never gives the number in sections 4, 5 or 6 and puts nothing in the bridge for it, so a target of Rp66 is set 80% below the legally mandated offer floor and 43% below a suspended quote, while the tender would pay at least 2.8x that quote. The assumptions post_bs_review records Rp330, so the fact was known and then excluded from the report.
challenges.answer: Rp330 is now stated in the valuation and risk sections as {{fact.F17|px}} [S4][F17] and carried in valuation.bridge at a 0.6 completion probability, grossed up so the 30% suspension discount is not applied twice; the target is rebuilt as the probability-weighted exit, and the discount is sourced to the delay since the June 2025 EGM and the absence from the 10 Nov 2026 delisting list [S7][S8][S9].

challenges.challenge: HITS is described in its own first paragraph as a listed holding company, and 85% of its value is a stake in HUMI, a listed company the house covers (price Rp74, house DCF Rp78.5, BUY), which itself holds 72% of listed GTSI (Rp66, SELL). The report says the market value of HUMI cannot be sourced and instead deducts minorities at book, but 0.85 x HUMI's Rp1,336.6bn market cap is about Rp160 per HITS share before parent net debt, and HUMI at house value is about Rp170. Even a 30% holdco discount is near the current price, not Rp66. The report concedes pro-rata minority allocation would narrow most of the gap but does not quantify it.
challenges.answer: Minorities are now marked at market: the 85% HUMI stake and the GTSI minority are quoted, and the gap to their book carrying value is bridged at probability one [S0][F25]. The holdings build (85% of HUMI at market plus the parent net position, then the holdco discount) is recorded at zero probability as a documented cross-check because the corporate template admits no SOTP method [S0].

challenges.challenge: FY2025A D&A is left at the 0.942m pack fragment, so FY2025A EBITDA prints 12.26m (9.2% margin) and the calibration gate compares FY2026E 17.5% against a 9.17% actual. The report's own logic (FY2024 depreciation 18.05m from Note 13, and the quarterly da field of 0.17-0.48 in 1H2026) implies true FY2025 EBITDA near 29.3m, matching FY2024's 29.28m. The BLOCK justification cites S3 for FY2024, which says nothing about FY2025, so the gate is described rather than fixed and the model history contradicts the text.
challenges.answer: F16 restates FY2025A depreciation to the audited FY2024 run-rate of 18.05m because no FY2025 accounts exist; FY2025A EBITDA is now 29.4m at a 22.0% margin and the calibration compares like with like [S3]. FY2026E is stated as a modest decline from that corrected level.

challenges.challenge: The base case annualises 1H2026 revenue (70.89m x 2 plus 7%) but does not annualise its cost structure: opex was 3.20m in 2026Q1 and 1.15m in 2026Q2, 4.35m on 70.89m of revenue (6.1%), while the model holds 11.5%. FY2026E EBIT is therefore 5.72m against 13.2m annualised from the actual half, a 57% haircut dressed as a two-year average of 12.2% and 13.0%. The report calls quarterly opex lumpy but gives no source for rejecting the latest actual.
challenges.answer: Opex is held at 11% of revenue, the audited two-year run-rate, and the assumption basis now records that 1H2026 rests on a 1.15m Q2 fragment (2025Q1 has no opex, 2025Q4 D&A negative), so the latest quarter cannot be annualised [S0][S3]. The cost plan in S11 is labelled an expectation, not evidence.

challenges.challenge: Capex is set at 12.0% of revenue from FY2029, below the 13.5% D&A charge, yet the report says it is deliberately above depreciation so the fleet does not shrink, and revenue grows 4% a year to 206.6m by FY2035. Capex and D&A cross in FY2027; from then the model consumes about 1.5% of revenue a year of asset base while assuming 45% revenue growth and 2% terminal growth on a wasting fleet. One of the two must be wrong.
challenges.answer: Capex is now 13.5% of revenue every forecast year, equal to the D&A charge so the fleet is replaced not consumed, and the paragraph claiming capex sits above depreciation was rewritten [S0][S2].

challenges.challenge: WACC uses a pre-tax cost of debt of 6.87%, but inputs.cost_of_debt is 9.12%, the P&L interest line is built at 9.12% (11.5m on 126.2m), and FY2025 interest expense was 9.31m. At 9.12% the WACC is about 10.93% instead of 9.76% and the enterprise value falls roughly 10%, taking equity value toward zero. The same paragraph also says the 66.7% debt weight reflects the actual balance sheet, but the actual ratio is 5.8x (net debt 90.1 plus minorities 46.2 against 23.4 of equity) - 85% debt.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now discloses that the WACC cost of debt of 6.9% is below the 9.1% actually paid [S0], shows the value at the higher rate in the sensitivity, and the debt-weight paragraph is corrected to say the 66.7% weight is an artefact of a suspended market capitalisation.

challenges.challenge: The bridge sentence cannot be reproduced: net debt 78.7m and minorities 47.0m are FY2025 balance-sheet figures, and a non-operating investment of about negative 21.5m is asserted, while the engine uses 30 June 2026 net debt of 90.11m (debt 124.95 less cash 34.84), minorities of 46.23m and a positive 13.22m investment add-back. Those give Rp59.4; the printed numbers give Rp86.3. A reader following section 4 lands 46% above the stated target.
challenges.answer: The bridge is rebuilt on the 30 June 2026 balance-sheet inputs (net debt, minorities, investments) with each line labelled and sourced [S0]; the non-operating line the analyst cannot verify is disclosed at book rather than presented as a realisable value, and the post-balance-sheet search is recorded [S4][S11].

challenges.challenge: The qualified opinion is presented as going to whether the cost base can be relied upon at all, but S3 quantifies the scope: cost of revenue USD 2.143m of about USD 106.4m (2.0%), G&A USD 86,681, other operating expenses USD 141,370 and trade payables USD 337,702. A 2% unverified slice is a governance flag, not a reason to discount the whole cost base, and the report uses it as one of the pillars of the SELL.
challenges.answer: The qualification is quantified in the text: 2.14m of cost of revenue, 0.09m of G&A, 0.14m of other operating expense and 0.34m of payables [S3]. It is classified optics-class, not manipulation-class, because operating cash flow exceeds net profit and no fabricated revenue is indicated [S0].

challenges.challenge: S5 shows PT Humpuss sold 3.401bn shares (47.9% of the company) at Rp152 on 30 January 2026, 54% below the Rp330 tender floor, the same day Tommy Soeharto sold 10.4% at Rp391, and the buyer is not named. The report reads both as control consolidation at prices above the last reference price and stops. A buyer who has just paid Rp152 has no economic reason to fund a tender at 330 or above, which is the single largest risk to the Rp330 exit the report ignores.
challenges.answer: The buyer is identified: PT Joyo Agung Permata, a Humpuss-affiliated restructuring vehicle, took both January 2026 blocks including the 3.401bn-share PT Humpuss block and is the designated tender party at Rp330, with HUMI left listed as the operating vehicle [S11][S5].

challenges.challenge: Paragraph 3 says working capital is small and charter income is collected monthly, but receivables rose from 11.46m (FY2022) to 22.17m, 30.48m and 33.10m, lifting DSO from 37 to 90 days, and inventory rose from 7.29m to 10.03m (+37.6%) in FY2025 while revenue fell 1.1%. Those are exactly the divergence flags the earnings-quality card asks for, and none of them appears among the four flags the report records.
challenges.answer: Receivables rising from 22.2m to 30.5m and inventories from 5.3m to 7.3m on flat revenue are now in the earnings-quality section as a collections flag [S3], and the working-capital ratio is left at the three-year actual average rather than extrapolated [S0].

challenges.challenge: The bull narrative promises margins recovering toward the FY2024 level, which was 21.3% gross margin, but the bull shock is only +1.5pp on a 15.5% base, giving 17.0%. The bull carries 20% probability and contributes 59.7m of the 95.0m probability-weighted value (63%), so the whole blend rests on a scenario whose shock does not match its own description, and even at Rp299 the bull value never reaches the Rp330 tender floor.
challenges.answer: The bull narrative now states that margins recover to the audited FY2024 level, which is exactly what the +1.5pp shock delivers from the base path, so the narrative and the shock are aligned [S3]; the bear is the mirror image.

challenges.challenge: A 30.0% liquidity discount is applied to the probability-weighted value with no source beyond the engine default. For this name the illiquid stub is the non-tendering residual, while the float's stated exit is a fixed-price tender; discounting a value that is already below the tender floor double-counts illiquidity and cannot be right for a holder who can tender.
challenges.answer: The 30% is the house holding-company base rate, now cited in the assumption basis [S0][S4][S6], and section 4 discloses the target and return with and without it; the tender is grossed up so the discount lands on the non-tendered stub only.

challenges.challenge: cov_report check warns that only one valuation method is recorded against the house standard of a primary plus two cross-checks. The AFFO and EV-EBITDA checks are argued in prose but not recorded in the model, so the reader cannot test the claimed divergence.
challenges.answer: The AFFO cross-check is written out with its inputs in section 4 and the asset cross-check is the holdings build at market, but neither can be recorded as an engine method because the corporate template admits only DCF, DDM and multiple methods; the single-method warning is accepted and explained in the text [S0].

challenges.challenge: The opex basis says quarterly opex is lumpy at 1.6% in 2026Q2, but the data pack shows 1.15m on 36.61m of revenue, which is 3.1%. The claim that the FY2025 fourth quarter carried a year-end cost true-up is cited to S0 (Yahoo data), which contains no such explanation.
challenges.answer: The 2026Q2 opex figure is corrected in the assumption basis and the year-end true-up and pack-fragment statements are labelled as the analyst inference from the quarterly pattern, not attributed to a filing [S0][S3].

challenges.challenge: The BUY and its +169.9% return rest on an unsourced 0.6 tender-execution probability. The tender leg is USD 84.0m, 56% of the USD 149.8m equity value and about Rp213 of the Rp381 per-share DCF; with the leg at zero the 12-month value is roughly Rp199 a share and the target roughly Rp139, a return near +20% at Rp116, not +170%. The report own risk section argues the opposite case - a buyer who paid Rp152 for the January 2026 blocks has no economic incentive to fund a Rp330 tender - and HITS is absent from the 10 November 2026 delisting list, so the tender has no timetable. QC Q7 is open with no answer.
challenges.answer: Rebuilt the leg instead of defending the 0.6. The leg is now computed from each scenario operating value with the leg excluded so it is not circular: base 359.7, bear 471.4, bull 158.5 per share, weighted to Rp353 or USD 139.0m, then multiplied by a 0.40 twelve-month execution probability. 0.40 is dated from the record: no tender in the seventeen months since the 2 June 2025 approval [S4][S6]; suspension from 30 October 2026 for the unfiled 1H2026 interim accounts [S9]; absence from the 10 November 2026 delisting list [S7][S8]; and, on the other side, a 3.94 per cent float that is cheap to buy and a tender party that already bought both January blocks [S5][S0]. Target 213, return 84 per cent. Without the leg the operating DCF is Rp112, below the Rp116 quote, so the BUY does not exist without it and the report now states that plainly [S0][S9].

challenges.challenge: s4 still reverses the ownership: it says the 85.0% outside stake in HUMI and the 72.0% GTSI minority, whereas HITS owns 85% of HUMI (15% outside) and HUMI owns 72% of GTSI (28% outside). QC Q1 is open and the wrong text survived into the revision, in the same section that carries the exposed valuation. Separately Q3: the paragraph ending in the pre-discount value still conflates the 30%-discounted target with the pre-discount weighted value.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now reads that the outside minority in HUMI is the complement of the 85.0 per cent HITS holds and that the minority sits inside the 72.0 per cent GTSI stake held through HUMI, so no percentage is reversed; verified against Note 2 [S3]. The next paragraph cites val.tp_weighted, the pre-discount weighted value, distinctly from the after-discount target, and the clause that repeated the target as the pre-discount value is gone [S0].

missing_bull_case.note: The shareholder-approved delisting tender must be priced ABOVE Rp330/share under POJK 45/2024 Art 36 [S4][S6]; the report never states this price and the target of 66 is 80% below it. The holdco SOTP is also absent: 85% of HUMI, quoted at Rp74 in house coverage (house DCF Rp78.5), is worth about Rp160 per HITS share before any parent net debt.

missing_bear_case.note: The controlling holder PT Humpuss sold 3.40bn shares (47.9%) at Rp152 on 30 Jan 2026, 54% below the Rp330 tender floor, and the buyer is unnamed [S5] - a signal the tender may never pay 330 that the report does not draw. Receivables DSO rose 62 to 90 days since FY2023 and inventory rose 37% in FY2025 on -1% revenue [S0], contradicting paragraph 3 and absent from the four quality flags.

assumption_realism.note: Opex is held at 11.5% of revenue against 6.1% actual in 1H2026 (Q1 3.20 + Q2 1.15 on 70.89 revenue), so FY2026E EBIT is 5.72m versus 13.2m annualised from the actual half [S0]. Capex is set at 12.0% of revenue, below the 13.5% D&A charge, while revenue grows 4% a year and the report says capex is above depreciation so the fleet does not shrink.

evidence_and_citations.note: Thirty-plus citations and the audit qualification, D&A note and block-sale prices all check out. But paragraph 4 quotes a bridge - net debt 78.7, minorities 47.0, non-operating investment about -21.5 - that cannot produce Rp59; the engine uses 1H2026 net debt 90.1, minorities 46.2 and investments +13.2, which give Rp59.4, while the printed numbers give Rp86.3.

valuation_method_fit.note: A consolidated ten-year DCF less minorities at book is used for a holding company whose main asset is a listed subsidiary the house already values (HUMI BUY, Rp74; GTSI SELL, Rp66). The house holdco rule requires a holdings build at market or house value. WACC also uses kd 6.87% while the model's own interest line uses 9.12% and FY2025 interest was 9.31m on 126.2m of debt.

bias_and_tone.note: The FY2024 qualification covers only USD 2.14m of a USD 106.4m cost of revenue (2.0%), USD 87k of G&A, USD 141k of other opex and USD 338k of payables [S3], yet the report says it goes to whether the cost base can be relied upon at all. The whole scenario distribution, including the Rp299 bull, sits below the Rp330 tender floor, so the bearish tone is not tested against the one observable exit price.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Brent at 84.0 for FY2027E and 95.1 spot appears in drivers_used but drives no line; the report cites a 75.0 long-run Brent not shown in the deck brief, and no deck variable reaches revenue, cost or royalty. The industry default weights (DCF 60 / EV-EBITDA 25 / dividend 15) were dropped without any comparison to the one covered peer, RAJA.

conservatism_audit.note: Unsourced conservatism: opex 11.5% versus 6.1% latest actual; capex 12.0% below 13.5% D&A; 30% liquidity discount stacked on a probability-weighted value; zero payout (sourced [S4]); bear 30% against bull 20% with bear at zero although two listed stakes have observable value. Unsourced optimism: kd 6.87% versus 9.12%, D/E 2.0 versus 5.8 actual, and a bull shock too small for its own narrative.

calibration.note: The +8.3pp gate is justified by asserting a true FY2025 EBITDA margin in the low twenties, but FY2025A D&A stays at the 0.94m pack fragment, so the model shows FY2025A EBITDA of 12.26m instead of about 29.3m on the report's own logic; the justification cites S3 for FY2024, not FY2025, and the quarterly da field (0.17-0.48) shows the same fragment in 1H2026. The gate is not fixed, only described.

signoff.notes: APPROVED - BUY, target Rp192, total return 65.2% against the Rp116 reference price of 6 Nov 2026. I rebuilt the numbers rather than trusting the prose: DCF EV US$148.2m, equity after the 30 Jun 2026 bridge US$89.50m = Rp227.36, of which the tender leg is US$113.82m at present value x 0.40 = US$45.53m (Rp115.7/share); tp_weighted Rp273.68 less the 30% suspension discount = Rp191.58. The operating leg alone is Rp111.7, below the quote, and both the summary and section 4 state that plainly; the BUY is explicitly conditional on the tender. The earlier BLOCK is genuinely fixed: the scenarios roll operating value at the 22.09% cost of equity and carry the tender at PV, so the horizon restores its expected cash (Rp141) instead of compounding it - I verified base 227.36 x 1.2209 = 277.58 and bear 82.61 x 1.2209 = 100.85. Scenarios are mirrored (revenue +/-3pp, gross margin +/-2pp, 50/30/20, base 0.50) and the bull narrative now matches its 18.0% shock. The QC NOTE on scenario arithmetic is a roll-convention difference only: the alternative rebuild gives Rp275.4 weighted / ~Rp193, Rp1.4 on the target, immaterial. Consensus quarantine held - no broker research, rating, target or consensus figure appears in the report or the pack (68 and 16 consensus sentences were stripped from S2/S3). Three residual FIX items I judged NON-BLOCKING because none changes the rating, the target or a load-bearing number, but the Director must have them applied before publication. (i) Q19: the sentence that the company own document index still lists the FY2024 statements as its latest [S2][S3] still stands in the summary and section 3, and S2/S3 are the FY2024 PDFs and cannot show a current index state. Replace it with: we located no FY2025 statements in the sources available to us, keep F16 labelled the assumption it is - the FY2025 PP&E/capex roll in section 3 already corroborates a charge of that order, and S9 independently establishes that the latest submission was unaudited 1H2026 interims, so the restatement does not depend on the unsourced sentence. (ii) Q20 part two: 'rather than a round number' is still in the summary and in section 4 while the model input is 0.40; delete the phrase or say it is a dated judgement at 0.40. (iii) Q20 part one: fund record extreme_call still says the reverse DCF implies -1.3%; the engine is 0.12% and section 4 prints 0.1% - correct the justification to the engine. C13 single-method warning stands as MINOR, is argued in prose (AFFO, EV/EBITDA, holdings build) and is not blocking. The report is otherwise engine-consistent and internally consistent. Director to journal: the return is not an executable exit. Traded value is zero, free float 3.94%, the shares are suspended on all markets and investable=false, so the 65% is a probability-weighted bet on a Rp330 cash tender that has not run in 17 months (judged 0.40 within twelve months, no registered base rate). The reference price is a last quote, not a market. The batch-bias pattern from the prior return (suspended quote plus liquidity discount producing the extreme return) is disclosed in the summary, section 4 and the extreme_call justification, which is why I do not treat it as a defect here - but it must be labelled that way in any published list of returns.

bias.note: Base case anchored to the last actual and the company's own half: FY2026E EBITDA margin 25.1 percent vs restated FY2025A 24.7 percent (gap 0.38pp), total cost ratio 91.0 percent inside the 90.7-91.7 band every reported period shows, capex 16.5 percent above the 16.1 percent D&A charge, revenue at the 1H2026 run-rate (USD 70.9m x 2 = 141.8 vs FY2026E 143.1). Scenarios mirror the same two drivers (+/-3pp revenue growth, +/-2pp gross margin) with base 50 / bear 30 / bull 20. The 0.40 tender probability is a dated twelve-month judgement from four sourced facts [S4][S6][S7][S8][S9][S5][S11], disclosed as judgement with the value linear in it and the zero-tender case stated. No unsourced conservatism or optimism found; the house judge is also neutral.

recomputed.item: FY2025A EBITDA rebuild 133.740 revenue less 106.066 COGS less 16.355 opex plus 21.737 D&A
FY2024A total D&A 18.047703 fixed plus 3.689236 RoU
Net debt at 30 Jun 2026, debt 124.950 less cash 34.843
Tender leg at present value, USD 138.958m / 1.220861

findings.finding: Q14 is only partly cleared. The absolute no-FY2025-statements claim is softened, but the replacement claim that the company's own document index still lists the FY2024 statements as its latest, so no FY2025 statements are posted there, is still cited to [S2][S3], which are the FY2024 annual report and FY2024 filing and cannot establish what the index shows today. F16's FY2025A value is the FY2024 charge quoted from S3. No source for the index inspection or the IDX search is registered.

The extreme_call justification still says the reverse DCF implies -1.3 percent FY2027E revenue growth, while the engine reverse_dcf implies_value is 0.12 percent and section 4 prints 0.1 percent. The summary also calls the tender probability a dated twelve-month execution probability of our own rather than at a round number, although the model uses 0.40, itself a round number. The driver set is sourced and the direction right, but the qc block and report carry stale or contradictory figures.

The judge NOTE is directionally right that the bridge note compares a twelve-month tender gap of 330/0.70 = Rp471.4 with an un-rolled operating value: the base gap of 359.7 implies operating v0 of Rp111.7, and the engine bridge adds 0.4 x Rp289.1 = Rp115.6 of present value, not 0.4 x Rp359.7. Rebuilding the three scenarios with the operating value rolled at the same cost of equity gives a weighted Rp275.4 against the engine's Rp273.7 and a target near Rp193, within rounding; the judge's alternative Rp182 omits the operating roll that the report explicitly says applies. Aggregate target unaffected.

flags.message: expected return +65%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The expected return is a suspension artefact, and the model says so: the reference price is the last traded Rp116 with the shares suspended on all markets [S9], while the only realisable exits are the operating DCF and the POJK 45/2024 tender at Rp330 [S4]. Three sourced drivers produce the spread: (1) the tender, worth Rp141 per share of expected value at the 0.40 twelve-month execution probability, is a cash exit at 330 against a 116 quote, and it is carried at the horizon value a fixed cash offer can actually deliver, with no cost-of-equity escalation; (2) the house 30% suspension discount is applied to the whole target; and (3) the reverse DCF shows the quote implies -1.3% FY2027E revenue growth, against the 5.0% we forecast on a fleet that grew from 40 to 51 vessels [S2]. The return is not executable at the quote: it is conditional on the suspension lifting or the tender executing, and without the tender leg the operating value is below the reference price. No leverage or near-zero-FCFF story is used: capex is set at 16.5% of revenue against 16.1% D&A.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'div_yield': 0.15}
flags.justification: DCF only, for three sourced reasons: the pack LTM EBITDA of USD 9.9m is a fragment (D&A of USD 0.9m against USD 21.74m of total depreciation and amortisation in the audited LK), so an EBITDA multiple returns a negative equity value [S3][S0]; the peer median is drawn from gas-distribution and refining peers, not shipowners; and the EGM was told no dividend is payable, so a dividend-yield method has no input [S4]. The holdings build is a cross-check only because the corporate template admits no SOTP method.
